text: Maybe a refresh of existing units is coming as well
groupUnder: Maybe a refresh of existing units is coming as well

contents:
The only place where the Nurgle range is bloated is the named Mortal Characters. For the rest, especially common units, Nurgle is relatively behind the other Chaos Gods.

For example, Khorne Infantry has "named" Warcry Unit, Bloodreavers, Blood Warriors, Skulltakers, Wrathmongers and Bloodletters. Tzeentch has "named" Warcry Unit, Kairic Acolytes, Tzaangors Warriors (ev. Enlightened on foot), Blue, Brimstone and Pink Horrors.

Nurgle Infantry only has Plaguebearer and "named" Warcry Unit, and Putrid Blightkings.

Pestigors Infantry really fits a niche in the Nurgle range, but I'm wondering if a "Magnificent sized" relase could imply some redesign instead of new units, for example modernized Plaguebearer ? Or we could have something like Nurgle Chaos Knights for the Harbingers to lead.

EDIT : a Pestigor character (Shaman ?) could fit the bill. And I'm still expecting Plastic Plague Toads for the Daemons range...

text: Boole gave us a series of posts detailing what happened in the unreleased book of Season of War: Gallet and Season of War: Andtor

contents:
Good evening. From this day forward, I shall be nothing but a storyteller

I will tell you a little story that I made up and there is absolutely no truth in it

Long long ago, perhaps in 2021?

There was once a series of stories, originally intended to be published in multiple volumes

In the first volume, the main character - shaman successfully mastered the method of summoning Incarnates and forged an alliance with the Orruks. Though the Incarnate he summoned was slain by a powerful woman, he remained undaunted and proceeded to summon further Incarnates of different kinds

In the second and subsequent volumes, the Shaman led his pallid Gor-kin companions in summoning Spider Incarnate

Meanwhile, the Dispossessed, leading the Dawnbringers, discovered the Khazalid ruins buried deep beneath the Ghur. This discovery held the potential to revive the lost civilisation of the Dispossessed

They also discovered countless ley lines stretching vertically and plunging deep into the Ghur. While battling the Spider Incarnate summoned by the Shaman and the new Gor-kin threat, they pressed onward with their excavation

Finally, the truth that astonished everyone was revealed: these vertically extending ley lines had long been targeted by rats. For centuries, these repulsive creatures had been executing some sinister scheme, and it was here they encountered a dreadful rat daemon - the daemon who orchestrated the entire stories

However, this story series was cancelled because the vast majority of its main characters were required to appear in another product line launched subsequently. Consequently, the models that had already been produced were unfortunately shelved

text: This refers very likely to shards or souls scaping from Slaneesh during the Broken Realms Morathi plot

contents:
It is worth noting that the cycle of reincarnation is an established lore of the elven pantheon.

That said, I personally don't think the elven deities of old will return or return exactly as they were.

Yet, sparkles of Morai-Heg indeed escaped. Is it that surprising if someone else also escaped?

text: Boole gave us a storytelling time about the elven pantheon and their possible comeback

contents:
Gooood Morning, storyteller's back

I heard that the goddess's followers donned armour forged from shadows and erected one new altar after another. 

Hold on, what's that? 

Returned ye be, O Mathlann, Khaine, and Kurnous! 

Thou tarriest overlong, Morai-Hag!

My heart foretold thy coming, Hoeth! 

Asuryan! Can it be thou too art restored? 

Remember, rumours are rumours, have a great day!

text: This refers very likely to shards or souls scaping from Slaneesh during the Broken Realms Morathi plot

contents:
It is worth noting that the cycle of reincarnation is an established lore of the elven pantheon.

That said, I personally don't think the elven deities of old will return or return exactly as they were.

Yet, sparkles of Morai-Heg indeed escaped. Is it that surprising if someone else also escaped?

text: All the above seem to indicate that Malerion will come soon! (5th edition?)

contents: It's opposite.
quotes: Still rather just have Malerion. I feel all this croneseer stuff is just kicking the ulgurothi/umbraneth can further down the road in favour of more witch elves.

text: A new tale by Boole talking about the upcoming Marshall Jorvan, the Freeguild Gargants, Cogforts, Crixxt and his deal with Bel'akor!
groupUnder: Cities of Sigmar vs Eshin Spearhead

contents:
Tahlia: Jorvan, d'you remember those battlemages? If we turn 'em into four new allies, d'you reckon our lads'll accept 'em?

Jorvan: Bloody hell, anythin's better than those Aelves what wrecked my homeland! Four new battlemages ain't nearly enough to drive out those sodding Aelves! We need more gargants, I swear on me sword and shield I'll wipe every last one of 'em out!

Tahlia: Steady on! It's the Skaven you should be after!

Jorvan: Right then, get me some Corgforts! That blighter Crixxit's got hold of Daemon Prince Be’lakor’s Shadow Power! Elsewise the little ****** could take down me whole army single-handed! Embergard needs more reinforcements, and sharpish!

Tahlia: You will get them……

text: Storytelling time for OBR by Boole. This time he hinted at four possible new units: Ossiarch Ruststalker, Golden Chariot/ Ossiarchstrike Chariot, Shooters with a third eye, and Blacktoof (Arkhan the Black?!)

contents:
Gooood Evening, the storyteller has returned.

In the distant realm of Shyish, legions beyond counting are being committed to the production lines — nay, verily, in numbers most prodigious!

They say the decapitation strike remains the most efficacious stratagem in all Warhammer lore, and Katakros has gained newfound insight into this art — perchance you have witnessed the Ossiarch Ruststalker?

Do you recall the tale of Katakros' own demise?

Were you to possess a formidable Ossiarchstrike Chariot, every difficulty would find its solution! Indeed — let that golden Chariot be rendered grander and more magnificent!

Why, pray tell, do so many in the Mortal Realms resort to the use of firearms? 'Tis most vexing! Had our warriors but the gift of a third eye, these wretched gunslingers would pose no threat!

The Blacktoof shall return — yet how distant lies that future? That, my friends, remains a secret veiled in shadow!



For the Tithe of Bones!



Remember, rumours are rumours, have a great day!

text: The above got a confirmation about the archers having three eyes and the "Ruststalker" being its own kit that would work as assassins

contents: I think he means the new OBR archers will literally have 3 eyes.

If the Ruststalker bit wasn't referring to Necropollis Stalkers or the rumored archers I could see them being something like a 5 model assassin unit which isn't a niche covered by anything else in the faction yet. Even though it seems to be shaping up to be a small wave, it at least sounds like it'll be better and less disappointing than what the Idoneth got this edition, possibly some actual new units and not just 3 infantry/on foot characters and an incarnate/manifestation.
quotes: when I think of third eye, only tzeetnch really comes to mind. "Warriors" and "gift" are also interesting choices of words here. It cant be that boole is sprinkling a little bit of hopium for tzeentch with obr here, is he?
